payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-07-02
payload.summary:
**Fable 5 storms back** and instantly hijacks the timeline; **Anthropic and OpenAI** keep pulling talent, attention, and workflow gravity into the labs; builders are moving from "can we build it" to "should we maintain it" as agents, dry runs, and sellable apps start looking more operational than experimental.

**Fable 5 一回归就把时间线点着了**；**Anthropic** 和 **OpenAI** 还在继续吸走人才、注意力和野心；圈子里的问题也变了，不再只是“能不能做出来”，而是“值不值得自己养着”，因为代理、dry run、可售卖应用这些东西，已经越来越像正经生产系统，不像试玩了。

sections.headline: **Every** on internal agents, **Codex**, and why build-vs-buy still matters | **Every** 聊内部代理、**Codex**，以及为什么“自建还是买现成”还没过时
sections.body:
**Every**'s consulting lead says **Codex** helped turn her daily stack into an operating system: email, meeting notes, inbound leads, dashboards, and CRM tasks now flow through an internal agent named **Claudie**. The update here is not novelty but routine. **Claudie** now runs in loops, evaluates itself, and handles SOP-driven work well enough to be treated like part of the team.

But the episode's sharper point is where the limits still bite. **Claudie** can execute against process, but it still needs oversight, taste, and someone to surface what's actually interesting in the data. That is why **Every** is still hiring humans in ops even as the agent gets better.

The most useful takeaway is the build-vs-buy reversal. They moved from a homegrown CRM stack glued together with Google Sheets to tools like **Attio** and **Asana**, not because AI failed, but because maintaining all the hidden logic was too expensive. Their argument is simple: AI can build almost anything now; that does not mean you should own the maintenance burden.

**Every** 的咨询负责人说，**Codex** 基本把她手里的工作流拧成了一套操作系统：邮件、会议记录、线索流转、仪表盘、CRM 事务，现在都能经过一个叫 **Claudie** 的内部代理。重点已经不是“新不新鲜”，而是它真的天天在跑。**Claudie** 会循环执行、做自我评估，按 SOP 干活已经像团队成员了。

但这期更有意思的地方，是边界仍然很硬。**Claudie** 很会按流程执行，可它还是需要人盯着，需要判断力，也需要有人把数据里真正值得看的东西拎出来。所以哪怕代理越来越能干，**Every** 还是在招真人做运营。

最实用的一层，是他们对“自建还是买现成”的态度变了。团队之前把 CRM 用 Google Sheets 和自制系统硬拼起来，后来还是换到了 **Attio** 和 **Asana**。不是因为 AI 不行，而是那些藏在细节里的规则太多，自己维护太费人。结论很直接：现在 AI 的确能把很多东西搭出来，但不等于你该把后续维护一并背上。

sections.headline: **Box** CEO says agent swarms will drive a 100x inference future | **Box** CEO 认为代理集群会把推理需求拉到 100 倍
sections.body:
If you’ve ever wondered why we will need 100X more AI inference in the future, and  what it’s going to be driven by, this is another good example. 

Devin pushes forward an idea of agentic mapreduce, which means we’ll now have swarms of agents that are processing large amounts of data (code) to handle tasks that humans never could have done before.

“Devin maps relevant signals across the repo, fans out focused agents over bounded shards, reduces their findings into one report, then verifies serious vulnerabilities in isolated sandboxes before marking them confirmed.”

In this case it’s code security, but there are tons of other use-cases in code and knowledge work. We see this at Box with customers that want to process and understand millions of documents for risk, insights, relationships, and more. This will play out in pharma, banking, and many other industries across all forms of unstructured data.

As an aside, these types of capabilities are generally only possible when you can deploy a variety of models (both the frontier and lower cost) because of the sheer amount of tokens that go into these use-cases. This is going to be a major value proposition for the applied AI layer.

如果你一直在想，为什么未来会需要 100 倍更多的 AI inference，以及需求到底会被什么拉动，这又是一个很好的例子。

Devin 正在推进一种 agentic mapreduce 的思路，也就是说，我们将会有成群的 agents 去处理海量数据（代码），完成过去人类根本做不了的任务。

“Devin 会在整个 repo 里映射相关信号，把有针对性的 agents 分发到边界清晰的分片上，再把它们的发现汇总成一份报告，最后在隔离沙盒里验证严重漏洞，确认之后再标记为已证实。”

这里是代码安全，但在代码和知识工作里还有大量别的用法。我们在 Box 也看到客户想处理和理解数百万份文档，从风险、洞察到关系抽取都是需求。制药、银行以及很多行业里，各种非结构化数据都会出现同样的事。

顺带一提，这类能力通常只有在你能部署多种模型时才成立，既要有前沿模型，也要有低成本模型，因为这些场景会吞掉大量 token。这会成为应用层 AI 的一个重要价值点。

sections.headline: Why **Lime** pulled off an IPO despite debt and survival doubts | **Lime** 背着债、还被怀疑撑不过一年，怎么还是 IPO 了
sections.body:
Fascinated by Lime going public - in an age where AI gets all the attention, how does a scooter company with $1B in debt pull off a successful IPO literally after expressing "substantial doubt" that they might not even survive the year?

* Impressive financial engineering - the IPO paid off the toxic loans and converted the rest to equity, so the slate is clean

* Uber owns 22% of Lime and refers riders directly to Lime, so obviously a great backstop and partner

* They've actually been FCF positive for 3 consecutive years with revenue growing nearly 30% YoY

* Something about being the last man standing and surviging the micromobility bloodbath (RIP Bird).  Never give up!

我对 Lime 上市这事很着迷。在一个注意力几乎全被 AI 吃掉的时代，一家背着 10 亿美元债务、而且前不久还明确表示对自己能不能活过今年存在 "substantial doubt" 的滑板车公司，到底怎么完成了一次成功 IPO？

* 财务操作确实厉害，IPO 把有毒贷款还掉了，剩下的转成股权，包袱一下轻了

* Uber 持有 Lime 22% 股份，还直接给 Lime 导流骑行用户，所以这显然是个很强的后盾和合作方

* 他们其实已经连续 3 年 FCF 转正，收入同比增长接近 30%

* 还有一点，就是它成了最后活下来的那家，熬过了整个微出行行业的大屠杀（RIP Bird）。别轻易认输。

This means having strong conviction and MASSIVE ambition if you choose to do it on your own.

My only counter to Xavi’s position will be that most VCs actually won’t make a lot of money.. at least life changing money. Some of them have actually deflected to the labs knowing this. Like any role the best ones will thrive and survive!

@OpenAI 和 @AnthropicAI 的人才漩涡只会越来越夸张。过去两个月里，我身边就有四个朋友离开了非常稳、非常成熟的岗位，转头进了这些实验室。

一边是去参与打造最重要的公司之一，一边又是 pre-IPO、还能拿到流动性，这个双重吸引力太难拒绝了。

这也意味着，如果你选择自己出来做，就得真的有很强的信念，还得有夸张的野心。

我唯一想反驳 Xavi 的一点是，多数 VC 其实赚不到很多钱，至少赚不到那种能改命的钱。有人也是看明白这一点，直接转去实验室了。跟任何行业一样，最强的那批人还是会活得很好。

sections.headline: A shot at default pessimism in **SF** | 朝 **SF** 里的默认悲观主义开了一枪
sections.body:
Every once in a while, I meet a very very smart but default-pessimistic person in SF. They are often from the growthy/wall-street part of the world.

And my first thought is: "Why would you want to be in this city? We run on optimism. Are you here to be a contrarian in your sadness?"

每隔一阵子，我都会在旧金山碰到那种非常非常聪明、但默认就是悲观的人。他们往往来自偏增长、偏华尔街的那一挂。

我脑子里第一个反应通常都是：“那你为什么还要待在这座城里？我们这里靠乐观驱动。你来这儿，是为了在自己的沮丧里当个唱反调的人吗？”
